note: verified=true means the source page was opened and read by a task chat. primary=true means a statute, regulator or standards body. Every number carries its source and the measure it came from. Densities are derived by the app as grams / (measure in mL); none are stored.
audience: General public. Every default below can be changed by the user where the result is shown, and the choice is remembered.
default_rule: Judgment, set at merge 1 (2026-11-19): the default convention is the primary source where one exists (manufacturer label or USDA), then a named authority. Exceptions: flours use the middle of published values (T04); a USDA value is skipped where it describes a different product. Sources never agree on flour, so the app always shows which value it used.
caveats: usda_hg72 was read through a fetch tool that summarises the page, from a university mirror. Spot-check its values against the PDF before public launch (task T11).
King Arthur lists water, milk, buttermilk, cream and sour cream at 227 g per cup, which is an 8-ounce rounding. USDA figures are used as the default for liquids.
Where a source does not state its cup size (measure says 'size unstated'), do not offer that value as a chip until the cup is confirmed.
T01 roster and T02 demand reports are not stored as files. They live in the project chats listed in project-journal.md.

reuse.note: Reported from each site's terms by T05; not a legal opinion. Sources not listed here were not checked. Justin decides before public launch (journal open question 1).

cup_standard.note: One-tap chip on cup and spoon results (T03). Default US customary is judgment: a typed cup means the recipe author's cup and most recipes found online are US.
